blocks.text: This chapter presents the concept of the evolution of life through the theories put forward by different scientists, and reviews the major evidence on which the most accepted theory of evolution is based.

blocks.title: Evolution
blocks.text: Evolution is the gradual change in the genetic makeup (allele frequencies) of a population over successive generations, which may lead to the formation of new species.

items: The universe and organisms did not always exist in their present form.
Today's organisms were not created at once.
They are the result of innumerable changes from lower to higher forms.

blocks.text: Those were the basic speculations of the concept in its earliest form. Evolution takes place through variation in organisms and natural selection: individuals with beneficial traits are selected to produce the next generations, while those with disadvantageous traits cannot, so the proportion of individuals with better traits in a population increases.
